newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae exec faults group's reorg plan.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae exec faults group's reorg plan.

text.p: Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) Executive Vice President Lydia Marshall on Wednesday demanded to be removed from a dissident shareholder group's proposed reorganization plans.
"Had you asked me, I would have told you that your plan was seriously flawed and ill-conceived," Marshall wrote in an April 16 letter to the Committee to Restore Value.
On Monday, Sallie Mae said most of its board recommends approving its privatization plan, which provides for a transition from a government-sponsored enterprise to a fully privatized company.

But the dissident group, which includes Albert Lord, last week announced a slate of 13 nominees for the board, which includes Edward Fox, Sallie Mae's former president and chief executive from 1973 to 1990. That group's nominees also include eight people who are presently Sallie Mae directors.
The dissident group last week reaffirmed its intention to hold a special meeting on May 9.
Marshall called the group's alternative reorganization plan an "off-the-cuff proposal."

"As shareholders subject your plan to serious scrutiny and analysis, I expect you to again back away from your key proposals just as you have backed away from you opposition to privatization," Marshall wrote.
